text: Old Behrman died. <break time="0.8s" /> In the hospital. <break time="0.8s" /> Two days later. <break time="0.8s" /> That afternoon. <break time="0.8s" /> Sue came to the bed. <break time="0.8s" /> Where Johnsy lay. <break time="0.8s" /> And put her arm around her. <break time="0.8s" /> I have something. <break time="0.8s" /> To tell you. <break time="0.8s" /> She said. <break time="0.8s" /> On the first stormy night. <break time="0.8s" /> The janitor found Mister Behrman. <break time="0.8s" /> In his room. <break time="0.8s" /> Helpless with pain. <break time="0.8s" /> His shoes and clothes. <break time="0.8s" /> Were wet through and icy cold. <break time="0.8s" /> They could not imagine. <break time="0.8s" /> Where he had been on such a terrible night. <break time="0.8s" /> Then they found a lantern. <break time="0.8s" /> Still lit. <break time="0.8s" /> And a ladder. <break time="0.8s" /> That had been dragged from its place. <break time="0.8s" /> There were also some brushes. <break time="0.8s" /> And a palette. <break time="0.8s" /> With green and yellow colors. <break time="0.8s" /> Mixed on it. <break time="0.8s" /> Look out of the window, dear. <break time="0.8s" /> At the last ivy leaf. <break time="0.8s" /> On the wall. <break time="0.8s" /> Did you not wonder. <break time="0.8s" /> Why it never moved. <break time="0.8s" /> When the wind blew. <break time="0.8s" /> Ah, darling. <break time="0.8s" /> It is Behrmans masterpiece. <break time="0.8s" /> He painted it there. <break time="0.8s" /> The night the last leaf fell.
